title: Positive-degree local alternating Čech contraction
statement: Let X be a scheme, U a finite family of opens indexed by Fin r, G an O_X-module, and i in Fin r. Let C be the integer extension of the alternating Čech sheaf complex for U and G, restricted to U i. There exist morphisms h_k:C^{k+1}→C^k for all integer k such that d_k h_k + h_{k-1} d_{k-1}=id on C^k for every k>0, with the canonical equal-index transport in the second composite. No equation at degree zero is required.

source.place: Tag 02FU (cohomology-lemma-covering-resolution), with the increasing-tuple convention of Tag 01FM

proof.text: Use the individual differential inner-inverse theorem to choose s_k with d_k s_k d_k=d_k. Set q_k=s_{k-1}d_{k-1}, inserting the canonical equal-index isomorphism. The complex identity d squared equals zero gives q_k d_k=0. Define h_k=s_k(1-q_k). These choices are internal to the existential proof; no definition is made from an arbitrary existence witness.

At positive degree k, use local exactness. The kernel lift of the incoming differential is epi (Mathlib ShortComplex.Exact.epi_kernelLift). Cancel it to show that its inner inverse acts as the identity on cycles. Apply this to a=1-d_k s_k, whose composite with d_k is zero by the inner-inverse equation. Thus a q_k=a. The proved private helper exact_inner_inverse_on_cycles performs the kernel lifting and epi cancellation.

Since q_{k-1}d_{k-1}=0, the incoming homotopy term is q_k. The outgoing term is d_k s_k(1-q_k). Expand a q_k=a to obtain d_k s_k-d_k s_k q_k+q_k=1. The Lean proof handles all equal-index transports with XIsoOfEq_hom_comp_d and d_comp_XIsoOfEq; no degree-zero equation is used.

lean.statement:
theorem alternatingCechSheaf_restrict_positive_contraction
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {r : ℕ} (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (G : X.Modules) (i : Fin r) :
    let F := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι
    let C := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      ((alternatingCechSheafComplex U G).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    ∃ h : ∀ k : ℤ, C.X (k + 1) ⟶ C.X k,
      ∀ k : ℤ, 0 < k → C.d k (k + 1) ≫ h k +
        (C.XIsoOfEq (show k = k - 1 + 1 by omega)).hom ≫
          h (k - 1) ≫ C.d (k - 1) k = 𝟙 (C.X k)
